lesen.title: Part 2
lesen.task: The people below all want to do something in the city this weekend. Read the eight descriptions a–h. Decide which place would be the most suitable for each person or group.

choices.text: City Farm Park: Feed the goats, meet the horses and play in our adventure playground. Our café serves fresh food from the farm. Open daily 9–5.
The Old Town Museum: Discover life in the city 300 years ago. Free tours with guides in historical costume every hour. Visit our gift shop for books and local crafts.
Riverside Climbing Wall: Indoor climbing for beginners and experts. Equipment hire included. Student price: £5, every day of the week.
Gallery of Contemporary Art: New exhibition of paintings by young European artists. Open late on Thursdays and Fridays until 9 pm, with talks by the curator at 7 pm.
Jazz at The Blue Room: Saturday night concert by the Ellis Quartet. After the show, join the band at the bar for a chat and signed CDs.
National Science Centre: Hands-on experiments for all ages and a special exhibition on robots. Café and picnic area. Closed on Mondays.
Grand Theatre: This month's musical 'Summer Nights' has been extended. Tickets from £35. Box office open 10–8.
Central Sports Centre: Swimming pool, gym and tennis courts. Membership required; day passes cost £25.

lesen.title: Part 3
lesen.task: Read the text and choose the correct answer a, b or c.

texts.title: A year without a smartphone
texts.body:
Last January, I made a decision that surprised my friends: I gave my smartphone to my brother and bought a basic phone that can only make calls and send texts. I was spending more than five hours a day on my phone, and I felt that I never had time for the things I really enjoyed.

The first few weeks were harder than I had expected. I kept reaching for my pocket when I was waiting for the bus, and I felt left out when my friends were sharing photos in group chats. I also had to buy a paper map, because I couldn't find my way around without one!

But after about a month, things started to change. I began reading on my way to college and finished more books in three months than in the whole previous year. I also started sleeping better, because I no longer looked at a screen before going to bed.

My friends were not always happy with my experiment. They had to call me instead of sending messages, and sometimes they forgot to tell me about plans. However, the friendships that mattered became stronger, because when we met, we actually talked to each other.

Now the year is over, and I have a smartphone again – I need it for my new job. But I have kept some of my new habits. I don't take my phone into my bedroom, and I switch off notifications for most apps. I would recommend the experiment to anyone, even if only for a month.

Lena

items.q: Why did Lena decide to stop using a smartphone?
options: She was using it too much.

items.q: What was difficult for Lena at the beginning?
options: She missed being part of online conversations.
She could not make phone calls.

items.q: After a month, Lena noticed that she…
options: spent more time with her brother.

items.q: How did the experiment affect Lena's friendships?
options: Her friends started using basic phones too.

items.q: What does Lena do now?
options: She uses her smartphone in the same way as before.
She has given up smartphones completely.
She limits how she uses her phone.

lesen.title: Part 4
lesen.task: Five sentences have been removed from the text. Choose the sentence a–h that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences which you do not need to use.

texts.title: Bees in the city
texts.body:
Ten years ago, very few people in London kept bees. Today, there are more than 5,000 hives in the city, on rooftops, in gardens and even on top of famous hotels. [1]

One reason for this is that cities can actually be good places for bees. [2] Parks, gardens and balconies are full of different flowers that bloom at different times of the year.

Many companies now have hives on their office roofs. [3] Some also give the honey to their staff or use it in their restaurants.

However, not everyone thinks this trend is positive. [4] Experts say that too many hives in one area can make it difficult for wild bees to find enough food.

So what can ordinary people do to help? [5] Planting flowers that bees like, such as lavender, is a simple way to support all kinds of bees.

choices.text: They say it helps them show customers that they care about the environment.
Bees are only active for a few weeks in summer.
Beekeeping has become one of the city's most popular hobbies.
You don't need to keep bees yourself.
Unlike the countryside, where farmers often grow only one type of crop, the city offers a wide variety of plants.
That is why many cities have banned beekeeping.
Honeybees compete with other insects for flowers.
Most hotels in London now sell their own honey.

hoeren.title: Part 3
hoeren.task: You will hear a radio interview with Ruby Clarke, who runs her own café. For each question, choose the correct answer a, b or c. You will hear the interview twice.
hoeren.audio:
Presenter: Today I'm talking to Ruby Clarke, who opened her own café at the age of twenty-two. Ruby, how did it all start?
Ruby: Well, I always loved cooking, but I actually studied business at university. During my studies I worked part-time in a bakery, and that's when I realised that food was what I really wanted to do.
Presenter: Was it difficult to open the café?
Ruby: Very! The hardest part was finding the money. Banks didn't want to lend money to someone so young, so in the end my family and some friends helped me. I paid them all back within three years.
Presenter: What makes your café special?
Ruby: Everything we sell is made that morning, and we only use ingredients from farms within fifty kilometres. Customers can taste the difference. We also have a pay-what-you-can table on Fridays for people who don't have much money.
Presenter: What's a typical day like for you?
Ruby: I start at five in the morning, baking bread with my assistant. The café opens at seven and it's busy until about two. In the afternoons I do the accounts and plan the menu for the next week.
Presenter: Any advice for young people who want to start a business?
Ruby: Don't be afraid to ask for help, and be ready to work very hard. But most importantly, choose something you really love – otherwise the long hours will feel impossible.

schreiben.title: Part 1 – Email
schreiben.task: Read this email from your English-speaking friend Sam: "Hi! I'm coming to visit your town next month for three days. What's the best time of year to visit? What should I see? Can you recommend a place to stay? Sam"
schreiben.prompt: Write your email to Sam. Write about 100 words and include all the points below.
points: say when the best time to visit is
schreiben.sample:
Hi Sam,

Great news that you're coming! The best time to visit is in late spring, because it's warm but not too hot, and there are fewer tourists than in summer.

You should definitely see the old castle on the hill – the view from the top is amazing. I'd also recommend the fish market by the harbour, especially early in the morning.

For a place to stay, try the Harbour Guesthouse. It's small and friendly, and it isn't expensive.

I'd love to meet you while you're here. Shall we have dinner together on your first evening?

See you soon,
Emre

schreiben.title: Part 2 – Article
schreiben.task: You see this announcement in an English-language magazine: "Articles wanted! My favourite way to relax. What do you do to relax? Why does it help you? Write an article and tell us!"
schreiben.prompt: Write your article in about 100 words and answer all the questions below.
points: when and where you do it
schreiben.sample:
Nothing relaxes me more than baking bread.

Every Sunday morning, before the rest of my family wakes up, I go into the kitchen, turn on some quiet music and start mixing flour, water and yeast. Then I wait for the dough to rise, which takes about an hour.

Why does it help? First of all, I can't look at my phone because my hands are covered in flour! I have to concentrate on what I'm doing, so I forget about school and stress. And at the end, the whole house smells wonderful and everyone has fresh bread for breakfast. Try it – you'll be surprised!

sprechen.title: Part 1 – Describe a scene
sprechen.task: Imagine you are looking at this photo: a family is having a picnic next to a lake on a sunny day. Describe what you can see: the people, the place, what they are doing and what the weather is like. Speak for about one minute.
phrases: In this photo I can see …
In the foreground / background there is …
sprechen.sample: In this photo I can see a family having a picnic next to a lake. There are two parents and two children, and they are sitting on a big red blanket on the grass. The father is cutting some bread, and the mother is pouring drinks. The children are laughing – I think they are playing a game. In the background there are some trees and a small boat on the water. The weather looks warm and sunny, so it's probably summer. Everyone seems relaxed and happy. It looks like a perfect day out.

sprechen.title: Part 2 – Discussion
sprechen.task: A friend wants to start a new hobby. Talk together about these ideas – learning an instrument, joining a sports club, painting, photography and cooking – and decide which would be the best for your friend.
sprechen.sample:
A: Let's start with learning an instrument. It's a great hobby, but it takes a long time to get good.
B: That's a good point. Joining a sports club might be better, because your friend could meet new people and keep fit.
A: True, but it can be expensive. What about photography? You only need your phone to start.
B: I like that idea. And cooking is useful too – you can use it every day.
A: Yes, but our friend already cooks a lot. I'd say photography, because it gets you outside and it's creative.
B: OK, shall we agree on photography, then?
A: Yes, let's do that.
